reader_question: Which House bills to rein in drug middlemen drew the same backers?
grade_line: Documented: bill records from the Library of Congress’s bill status files
title: Of 10 House bills whose titles name pharmacy benefit managers, H.R. 6609 and H.R. 6610 shared the most backers, 34 members.
measure_line: Members who sponsored or cosponsored both bills of a pair, House bills of the 119th Congress whose titles name pharmacy benefit managers, in order of introduction, February 4, 2025 to September 14, 2026; an arc’s width is its count
notes: Pharmacy benefit managers run prescription drug benefits for insurers and employers. We searched every bill of the 119th Congress in the Library of Congress’s files of November 11, 2026 for a title, official, short or popular, that names “pharmacy benefit manager” or “PBM”, and found 10 House bills and eight Senate bills.

A representative cannot back a Senate bill, so the chart draws the House, the chamber with more such bills. The Senate’s eight are S. 526, S. 882, S. 3345, S. 3349, S. 3549, S. 3729, S. 3822 and S. 4509.
A backer is the sponsor or a cosponsor who did not withdraw. Two bills that share backers drew some of the same members, and their texts may still differ.
alt: Ten House bills on a line in order of introduction, with 33 arcs joining each pair that shares a sponsor or cosponsor, each arc as wide as its count. H.R. 6609 and H.R. 6610, introduced the same day, share 34 backers, the most; H.R. 4317 shares 19 with each of them; the other 30 pairs share one to six.
chart_notes: The pair the title names, H.R. 6609 and H.R. 6610, is in the text’s ink; every other arc is gray. The chart draws the widest arcs first, so the narrow ones stay in view.

table.caption: Pairs of House bills naming pharmacy benefit managers that share a sponsor or cosponsor, 119th Congress
